variables.name: requested_type
variables.description: TokenType passed to CreateToken/NewPayload (1 = access, 2 = refresh).

variables.name: duration_negative
variables.description: The duration passed to token creation is negative, so the payload is born expired.

variables.name: issued_type
variables.description: The Type stamped into the (most recently built) token payload; payload.Type.

variables.name: expected_type
variables.description: TokenType the verifier demands (tokenType argument of VerifyToken / Payload.Valid). Fixed to access (1) by authMiddleware and authorizeUser, to refresh (2) by renewAccessToken; chosen by the caller for direct calls.

variables.name: token_expired
variables.description: The presented token's ExpiredAt is in the past.

variables.name: token_authentic
variables.description: The presented token was sealed/signed by this maker with its key (PASETO decrypts; JWT verifies with HMAC). False for a hand-built alg=none JWT.

variables.name: claims_are_payload
variables.description: Parsed JWT claims are a *Payload (always, since ParseWithClaims is given &Payload{}).

variables.name: payload_valid
variables.description: Payload.Valid(expected) returned nil: type matches and not expired.

variables.name: verify_failed
variables.description: VerifyToken returned an error (ErrInvalidToken or ErrExpiredToken).

variables.name: authorize_failed

variables.name: token_create_failed

variables.name: auth_metadata_present

variables.name: header_has_two_fields

variables.name: scheme_is_bearer

variables.name: role_permitted

variables.name: caller_is_banker

rules.name: A token is accepted only for the type it was issued as
consequences: Payload.Valid returns ErrInvalidToken before looking at expiry
every caller treats it exactly like any other verification failure

rules.name: Creation stamps the requested type into the payload
consequences: login issues one access (1) and one refresh (2) token; renew issues an access token

rules.name: Entry points fix the expected type
Expired tokens are rejected (after the type check for PASETO; by the JWT library before the type check for JWT)
consequences: PASETO: Valid returns ErrExpiredToken only if the type matched
JWT: ParseWithClaims fails with ErrTokenExpired and VerifyToken returns ErrExpiredToken; Valid is never reached

rules.name: Tokens not sealed by this maker are invalid
consequences: VerifyToken returns ErrInvalidToken without calling Valid

rules.name: Verification failure ends the request as unauthenticated
consequences: authorizeUser errors so UpdateUser returns codes.Unauthenticated (*status.Error)

rules.name: Bearer header required before any token work
consequences: reject without calling VerifyToken (HTTP 401 / gRPC Unauthenticated)

rules.name: UpdateUser: valid fields, and banker or self

unknowns.what: Equality of token types at call boundaries
unknowns.why: The only boundary facts are is_set/changed_from/size/bool; the tokenType argument digests (#35ddf6 vs #018508) cannot be bound to integer variables, so issued_type and expected_type are carried by transitions and scenario facts and checked only through br:8d10f2f9b136 outcomes.

unknowns.what: Which token a verification refers to
unknowns.why: issued_type/token_expired/token_authentic describe a single 'current token'. Login creates two tokens (access then refresh) and renew verifies one and creates another; tracking per-token identity (the refresh token later presented to renew) needs relation-valued variables or item identity, which are not available. A scenario that creates two tokens and verifies the first would be mis-predicted.

authorizeUser, authMiddleware, renew and login call the Maker interface; procedures name PasetoMaker because servers are observed with PASETO. A JWT-backed server would route to JWTMaker.VerifyToken, whose type check runs after the library's expiry check (ordering differs: expired+wrong-type is ErrExpiredToken for JWT, ErrInvalidToken for PASETO).
Not required; hasPermission is modeled only by its bool result (role_permitted), the loop over accessibleRoles is iteration over a collection.

unknowns.what: HTTP login/renew, gRPC LoginUser/CreateUser runtime behavior
unknowns.why: No shown test exercises them; their decisions are proposed from source only, and exit kinds for gRPC error paths are assumed to be *status.Error.
